questions.answer: Michigan argued that the Big Ten would be acting too hastily in suspending Jim Harbaugh or punishing Michigan before a full NCAA investigation is completed, that the university has not had a chance to review all evidence and respond, that Pettiti should not have unilateral authority to punish without a completed investigation and response from the Compliance and Reinstatement Committee, that there is no evidence Michigan athletics personnel committed the allegations, that the electronic recordings rule is limited to field equipment used by the institution for the game it is currently playing, that Michigan has only heard a summary of second- and third-hand information, that Stalions' efforts likely were not meaningful given sign decoding by other universities, and that the information obtained is at most a reflection of publicly and permissibly obtainable information and highly dubious to have a material effect on the integrity of the competition.

triples.o: The Big Ten would be acting too hastily in suspending Harbaugh or levying any punishment toward Michigan before the completion of a full NCAA investigation.
The university has not had the chance to review all the evidence and respond, which oversteps the due process allowed for Michigan.
Pettiti should not have unilateral authority to punish violations without first having a completed investigation and then a response from the Compliance and Reinstatement Committee.
There is nothing it is aware of to claim athletics personnel at Michigan committed the allegations.
The rule pertaining to electronic recordings of games is limited to the use of field equipment used by the institution for the game it is currently playing.
Michigan has not seen much evidence, but rather has just heard a summary of second- and third-hand information.
Given the use of sign decoding by other universities, there is little reason to believe Stalions' efforts proved meaningful.

The information obtained is at most a reflection of information that teams can and easily do obtain through public and permissible sources, and because of that it is highly dubious that Stalions' observations would have a material effect on the integrity of the competition.
